text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish tax minister Carsten Koch recognises that it will only be practically possible for the state and local authorities to recover about one third of the 36 billion crowns owed by Danes to the tax authorities at national and local level.

--Denmark's Employers' Federation urges that employees should only qualify for early retirement pensions at the age of 63, as opposed to 60 as is the current practice, criticising the present age limit as too low. The Danish government is resisting any talk of doing away with early retirement. The number of Danes on early retirement benefits will have doubled by 2008 if the present age limit is not lifted, it is estimated.

--Denmark's Social Democrat-led minority government and its allies survived attempts in parliament by the centre-right opposition led by the Liberals and Centre Democrats to drop housing taxes. The latest Danish economic Wise Men's report called on the contrary for these taxes to be increased.
--Monopoly telecommunications group Tele Danmark has bowed to criticism from competitors and is now to allow them to set their own tariffs for conventional telephony using its network.

--Danish aviation spares distributor Satair is to be the first new company to be listed on Copenhagen Stock Exchange this year. There is great interest in the share issue which is expected to be vastly oversubscribed due to its low price and attractiveness to investors.
